title: Praxis Special Education: Teaching Students with Intellectual Disabilities (5322) - 200 Source Questions + 300 Guided Review
description: Contains 200 original source questions, 0 assistant-authored independent practice questions, and 300 source-derived guided-review activities. The assistant audit found 101 distinct independent content kernels. Two 100-item diagnostics, an exact-blueprint 120-item simulation, detailed feedback, native learning support, and case-study decision practice for preschool-through-grade-12 ID specialists.
contentReview: Assistant audit completed: 200 independent-practice items contain 101 distinct content kernels and 99 parallel variants under the normalized test. 300 additional activities are guided reasoning transformations, not independent exam questions. The 500-distinct-question target is not met.
simulationLabel: 120-question Teaching Students with Intellectual Disabilities simulation
officialCaseStudyNote: The official exam includes some selected-response questions based on an approximately 500-word case study.
disclaimer: Independent preparation material, not affiliated with or endorsed by ETS or AAIDD. Results are not official forms, scaled scores, pass predictions, licenses, diagnoses, eligibility, placement, adaptive-behavior determinations, medical or legal advice, or substitutes for individualized assessment and current requirements.

domains.label: Development and Characteristics of Students with Intellectual Disabilities
Planning and Managing the Learning Environment

items.prompt: In reviewing early developmental records, a kindergarten teacher notices that one child reaches several language milestones later than classmates. What is the most appropriate first interpretation?
choices: Broad developmental patterns allow wide variation, so the team should gather multi-source evidence across settings before drawing conclusions.
Falling below the typical classroom average on language milestones establishes a developmental disability that warrants formal eligibility.
The team should assign a provisional disability label promptly so specialized speech-language interventions can begin before gathering family input.
Chronological age norms become uninformative once a child trails classmates, so expectations should be based on informal adult impressions instead.
items.rationale: Milestones provide useful reference points, not stand-alone diagnoses. Educators should document functioning across domains, contexts, and time and involve qualified team members before attributing a pattern to disability. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Correct. Milestones provide useful reference points, not stand-alone diagnoses. Educators should document functioning across domains, contexts, and time and involve qualified team members before attributing a pattern to disability. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
Classroom averages reflect one peer group rather than a diagnostic standard, and early language variation can stem from experience, exposure, or home-language patterns rather than a disability.
Assigning a provisional disability label before multidisciplinary evaluation and family input bypasses IDEA safeguards and risks misidentifying typical developmental variation as an impairment.
Chronological age remains an essential benchmark for interpreting developmental expectations and selecting age-respectful instructional routines, even when a learner needs targeted supports.

items.prompt: In contrasting classroom contexts, a student solves multistep problems during small-group instruction but rarely begins the same work during a noisy whole-class period. What should the teacher examine first?
choices: Conclude that the student has not yet retained the underlying academic skill and re-teach the lesson from the beginning.
Compare task demands, environmental conditions, supports, and performance across both settings.
Lower the academic complexity of the independent assignment so the student can finish without using classroom supports.
Treat the drop in task initiation during the busier period as willful avoidance and add a stricter compliance consequence.
items.rationale: Performance reflects an interaction among learner skills, task demands, supports, and context. Comparing conditions can identify a removable barrier before the team changes expectations or infers a stable trait. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Because the student already demonstrates the skill in the structured setting, the gap points to contextual or support barriers rather than a loss of conceptual understanding.

Correct. Performance reflects an interaction among learner skills, task demands, supports, and context. Comparing conditions can identify a removable barrier before the team changes expectations or infers a stable trait. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
Reducing academic complexity lowers expectations unnecessarily when the learner has already shown the ability to meet the target under supportive environmental conditions.
Interpreting context-dependent disengagement as intentional defiance overlooks sensory, organizational, or initiation barriers that can be addressed proactively through environmental supports.

items.prompt: To plan proactive self-regulation supports, a teacher wants to understand a learner’s self-regulation needs. Which information is most useful?
choices: A single global behavior rating scale completed by a previous teacher at the start of the school year.
The student’s primary disability eligibility category paired with a general list of typical classroom accommodations.
Current observations of triggers, strategies used, recovery patterns, and successful routines.
Whole-class averages showing how long most classmates sustain independent work without requesting teacher support.
items.rationale: Self-regulation is best understood through specific, current observations of what precedes difficulty, how the learner responds, which strategies help, and whether patterns differ by setting or task. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: An outdated global rating summarizes broad impressions from another context and fails to identify the specific triggers, warning signs, and calming strategies relevant to current routines.
Eligibility labels describe broad qualifying criteria rather than individual regulation profiles, so relying on category lists misses the learner’s actual antecedents and effective coping tools.

Correct. Self-regulation is best understood through specific, current observations of what precedes difficulty, how the learner responds, which strategies help, and whether patterns differ by setting or task. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
Peer-group averages show general classroom norms but do not reveal what overwhelms this individual student or which environmental adjustments help restore engagement.

items.prompt: When evaluating multilingual student performance, a multilingual learner has difficulty following rapid oral directions in English but demonstrates the task after a peer models it. Which interpretation is best?
choices: Difficulty demonstrating understanding through rapid English oral tasks provides sufficient evidence to suspect an intellectual disability.
Peer modeling and visual representations should be removed during checks so the teacher can measure the student’s true academic mastery.
Information about how the student performs in the home language is outside school accountability and should be set aside during planning.
Language access may affect how knowledge is shown, so gather culturally and linguistically appropriate evidence.
items.rationale: Difference is not disability. The team should distinguish language acquisition and access from disability by using multiple methods, appropriate language supports, and information about performance in the learner’s languages. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Limited proficiency in rapid English instructions reflects second-language processing demands, not impaired intellectual functioning; accurate demonstration via modeling or visuals argues against cognitive deficit.
Stripping away modeling or visual supports confounds English language load with content mastery, making assessment data less valid rather than more accurate.
Home-language performance is crucial evidence for distinguishing language acquisition from disability and helps educators build on concepts the student already understands.

Correct. Difference is not disability. The team should distinguish language acquisition and access from disability by using multiple methods, appropriate language supports, and information about performance in the learner’s languages. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.

items.prompt: While selecting functional instructional materials, a middle school student with an intellectual disability is embarrassed when an adult uses age-inappropriate materials for a functional routine. What principle should guide revision?
choices: Use age-respectful materials while adapting task steps and supports to current learner needs.
Select instructional materials strictly by developmental age estimate so the formatting matches early-childhood readiness charts.
Postpone functional and daily-living instruction until the student achieves independent mastery on grade-level academic standards.
Assign helpful classmates to perform the functional routine for the student so embarrassing instructional materials are unnecessary.
items.rationale: Instruction can be individualized without sacrificing dignity. Materials and contexts should be chronological-age respectful, while prompts, task steps, and response modes are adapted to the learner’s present performance. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Correct. Instruction can be individualized without sacrificing dignity. Materials and contexts should be chronological-age respectful, while prompts, task steps, and response modes are adapted to the learner’s present performance. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.

Delaying essential daily-living instruction until full grade-level mastery denies functional independence and violates the balance between academic access and life-skills preparation.
Having peers complete the routine removes authentic learning opportunities, fosters dependence, and prevents the student from building self-determined functional skills.

items.prompt: To promote durable skill transfer across school routines, a student performs a social routine only with one familiar adult. Which plan best promotes generalization?
choices: Continue drilling the skill in the original instructional setting until accuracy stays high across several additional months.
Teach across planned variations in people, materials, and natural settings, then fade prompts.
Introduce multiple unrelated social and communication targets simultaneously so the student practices broader flexibility right away.
End direct instruction once mastery appears in the familiar setting and monitor whether transfer emerges spontaneously over time.
items.rationale: Generalization is more likely when instruction deliberately varies relevant people, materials, and settings, reinforces the skill in natural routines, and gradually transfers stimulus control away from adult prompts. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Over-practicing in one controlled setting with one adult strengthens narrow stimulus control and rarely transfers without deliberate instruction across natural partners and environments.

Correct. Generalization is more likely when instruction deliberately varies relevant people, materials, and settings, reinforces the skill in natural routines, and gradually transfers stimulus control away from adult prompts. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
Adding unrelated targets at the same time increases cognitive load and interferes with consolidating the specific cue-response link the student needs to transfer.
Hoping for spontaneous transfer—often called train-and-hope—frequently fails for learners who need explicit programming across settings, natural cues, and reinforcement contingencies.

items.prompt: When drafting an objective learner profile, a team is writing a learner profile. Which statement is most useful for planning?
choices: The student performs at a low-functioning developmental level across most structured and unstructured school routines.
Because the student has an autism diagnosis, the student prefers fixed classroom schedules and dislikes unexpected changes.
The student completes a two-step visual routine independently and needs one verbal cue when steps change.
The student operates at a developmental stage several years below same-age classmates in daily classroom independence.
items.rationale: Objective descriptions identify a demonstrated strength, a specific condition, and the support needed. Global labels and assumptions based on category do not tell the team what to teach or how to measure change. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Broad deficit labels such as low-functioning are non-specific, lack measurable baseline data, and fail to show what the student can already do or which prompts help.
Inferring preferences from a diagnostic label stereotypes the learner instead of documenting observable classroom performance, specific conditions, and effective supports.

Correct. Objective descriptions identify a demonstrated strength, a specific condition, and the support needed. Global labels and assumptions based on category do not tell the team what to teach or how to measure change. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
Age-equivalent estimates oversimplify uneven skill profiles and do not specify the observable behaviors or instructional cues the team needs to write measurable goals.

items.prompt: Following major family or housing transitions, a learner’s participation drops after a recent family move and change in transportation. How should the school respond?
choices: Attribute the sudden drop in classroom participation to progression of the student’s underlying disability profile.
Recommend moving the student to a more restrictive special education classroom so academic expectations can be reduced.
Keep classroom planning focused on curriculum pacing because housing and transportation factors fall outside school instruction.
Weigh environmental disruptions alongside disability needs and coordinate supports respectfully.
items.rationale: Development and learning are influenced by environmental as well as biological factors. A responsive team gathers context, protects privacy, stabilizes access, and avoids treating a situational change as proof of a new disability need. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Blaming an acute performance drop on an existing disability overlooks clear situational stressors such as disrupted sleep, attendance, or routines that require stabilization supports.
Changing placement to a more restrictive setting violates LRE principles when the decline coincides with temporary external disruptions rather than an inability to learn with supports.
Ignoring major environmental stressors misses actionable school-based resources—such as flexible check-ins, McKinney-Vento coordination, and counseling—that directly affect access to learning.

Correct. Development and learning are influenced by environmental as well as biological factors. A responsive team gathers context, protects privacy, stabilizes access, and avoids treating a situational change as proof of a new disability need. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.

items.prompt: Before reducing academic expectations after a single low probe, a teacher records one difficult morning and says a student has lost a previously learned skill. What evidence is needed before changing the program?
choices: Gather repeated observations and work samples under representative conditions and compare them with baseline data.
Revise the instructional program right away because the most recent classroom observation reflects the student’s current true level.
Review the student’s disability classification report to confirm whether regression is commonly associated with that label.
Postpone gathering additional evidence until the scheduled annual IEP meeting so classroom routines remain uninterrupted.
items.rationale: A single observation may be affected by health, context, fatigue, or task features. Repeated measures and comparison with baseline information support a more reliable decision about whether performance truly changed. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Correct. A single observation may be affected by health, context, fatigue, or task features. Repeated measures and comparison with baseline information support a more reliable decision about whether performance truly changed. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
A single low session is vulnerable to fatigue, illness, distraction, or testing glitches and provides insufficient reliability to justify major programmatic changes.
General category expectations cannot verify whether an individual learner experienced genuine skill regression; direct longitudinal performance data are required.
Waiting until an annual review without collecting follow-up probes leaves the team unable to tell whether the dip was temporary or signals an urgent instructional need.

items.prompt: When an academic profile shows strong areas alongside targeted needs, a student with a specific learning disability reads grade-level text accurately but cannot organize written paragraphs. Which response is best?
choices: Deliver uniform remedial instruction across all core academic subjects so the student receives consistent skill reinforcement.
Target the documented area of academic need while preserving strengths in unaffected subjects.
Interpret the persistent academic bottleneck as evidence of broadly limited cognitive ability across every learning domain.
Assign an instructional aide to complete the demanding academic steps so the student can keep pace with class assignments.
items.rationale: Specific learning disabilities can affect particular psychological processes and academic skills unevenly. Instruction should be based on the learner’s actual pattern of strengths and needs, not a global assumption. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Applying blanket remediation across strong subjects wastes instructional time, lowers engagement, and ignores the defining uneven skill profile typical of specific learning disabilities.

Correct. Specific learning disabilities can affect particular psychological processes and academic skills unevenly. Instruction should be based on the learner’s actual pattern of strengths and needs, not a global assumption. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
Specific learning disabilities affect targeted processing and academic skills rather than overall intellectual capacity, so inferring broad cognitive limits misinterprets the learner’s profile.

items.prompt: To support sensory predictability during school safety routines, a student with autism covers their ears during fire-drill announcements and then misses directions. Which support is most responsive?
choices: Treat covering the ears and missing directions as task refusal and apply standard classroom behavior consequences.
Excuse the student from participating in future schoolwide drills or timed transitions to avoid triggering sensory distress.
Build a predictable warning and accessible cueing routine while teaching the student how to use it.
Continue using loud, unannounced signals without preparation so the student gradually desensitizes through repeated exposure.
items.rationale: Sensory and communication needs can affect access and behavior. A predictable warning, accessible direction, and taught coping or communication response support participation while preserving safety requirements. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Treating sensory overload as willful defiance misreads a neurobiological access barrier and can escalate distress without teaching an effective safety or transition response.
Excluding the student from safety drills or transitions undermines safety preparedness and reduces inclusive participation when proactive sensory supports can enable success.

Correct. Sensory and communication needs can affect access and behavior. A predictable warning, accessible direction, and taught coping or communication response support participation while preserving safety requirements. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
Unprepared exposure to painful or overwhelming auditory stimuli risks trauma and escalation rather than building self-regulation or reliable response to emergency directions.

items.prompt: When analyzing how organizational supports affect starting assignments, a student with ADHD begins work when directions are chunked and a checklist is visible. What does this pattern suggest?
choices: The student already mastered the self-management skills needed and had been choosing not to start earlier assignments.
Adding checklists and interim milestones has lowered the rigor of the grade-level academic standard being assessed.
The student’s uneven project completion reflects limited intellectual understanding of the content rather than self-regulation.
Executive-function scaffolds are strengthening task initiation, planning, and self-monitoring.
items.rationale: ADHD may affect executive functions such as initiation, working memory, inhibition, and organization. External structures can support performance without changing the learning target or implying weak ability. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Responding well to external structure is a hallmark of executive-function support needs, not evidence of intentional noncompliance or lack of motivation.
Chunking directions and setting interim checkpoints support organization and initiation while keeping the underlying academic content and rigor intact.
Completing the same content accurately once tasks are structured demonstrates intact conceptual capability paired with executive-function barriers to independent planning.

Correct. ADHD may affect executive functions such as initiation, working memory, inhibition, and organization. External structures can support performance without changing the learning target or implying weak ability. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.

items.prompt: In reviewing context-dependent peer-group conflict, a student with an emotional or behavioral disability argues mainly during unpredictable peer-group tasks. What perspective is most useful?
choices: Analyze interactions among the learner, task structure, peers, expectations, and consequences.
Expect the same level of emotional conflict across every school setting because the disability resides within the student.
Conclude that classmates’ interpersonal habits are the sole cause of the student’s behavioral difficulties during group work.
Replace peer-group and cooperative learning tasks with independent seatwork for the remainder of the academic year.
items.rationale: An ecological perspective considers how behavior emerges through interactions between the learner and the environment. Context-specific data can guide prevention, instruction, and reinforcement of more effective responses. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Correct. An ecological perspective considers how behavior emerges through interactions between the learner and the environment. Context-specific data can guide prevention, instruction, and reinforcement of more effective responses. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
Assuming behavior is invariant across contexts ignores the clear contextual contrast shown in the scenario and misses preventive instructional levers.
Blaming peers alone oversimplifies a reciprocal interaction and ignores how clear roles, expectations, and taught social skills can improve participation.
Eliminating collaborative opportunities permanently removes vital social-learning contexts and restricts access to inclusive peers instead of teaching structured participation.

items.prompt: While evaluating daily-living and learning support needs, which information is essential when considering educational needs associated with intellectual disability?
choices: A standardized oral reading fluency and comprehension score collected during a single school screening window.
Combined data on cognitive functioning and adaptive behavior across conceptual, social, and practical domains.
Medical history records and physical growth measurements gathered from the student’s primary health-care provider.
Anecdotal teacher ratings describing the student’s adherence to rules inside one general education classroom.
items.rationale: Intellectual disability involves limitations in intellectual functioning and adaptive behavior. Educational planning therefore considers functional conceptual, social, and practical performance across relevant environments. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: A single academic reading measure cannot capture broader intellectual functioning or everyday social and practical adaptive skills needed to plan comprehensive supports.

Correct. Intellectual disability involves limitations in intellectual functioning and adaptive behavior. Educational planning therefore considers functional conceptual, social, and practical performance across relevant environments. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
Medical history may inform health accommodations, but it does not document cognitive functioning or adaptive performance across school, home, and community settings.
Informal impressions from one classroom omit cross-setting adaptive evidence and standardized cognitive information required for accurate educational planning.

items.prompt: When vocal articulation lags behind academic understanding, a student grasps grade-level ideas yet struggles to speak clearly. What is the most appropriate instructional assumption?
choices: Simplify the cognitive complexity of class questions so the student can participate with brief, low-demand responses.
Speak for the student during whole-class discussions so the pacing of the lesson remains smooth for classmates.
Presume competence, support an accessible response mode, and separate speech production from content mastery.
Require spoken oral answers during formal checks so the student gets daily practice in expressive articulation.
items.rationale: A communication disability can limit how knowledge is expressed without indicating limited understanding. Accessible response modes and adequate wait time help the student demonstrate the intended construct. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Lowering cognitive rigor confuses speech-production barriers with intellectual capacity and deprives the learner of grade-level conceptual challenge.
Answering on the student’s behalf silences the learner’s voice, denies authentic communication practice, and prevents accurate assessment of what the student knows.

Correct. A communication disability can limit how knowledge is expressed without indicating limited understanding. Accessible response modes and adequate wait time help the student demonstrate the intended construct. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.

items.prompt: In coordinating services for co-occurring visual and motor conditions, a learner has both a visual impairment and a motor disability. How should the team plan access?
choices: Attach standard classroom accommodations for each separate disability label without trialing how they work together.
Prioritize accommodations for the student’s primary eligibility category while keeping other routines unchanged.

Evaluate how the combined needs interact in each task and coordinate supports across specialists.
items.rationale: Co-occurring disabilities may interact in ways that are not captured by treating each label separately. Collaborative task analysis and trials show how combined access, communication, positioning, and health supports function. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Stacking isolated accommodations without testing them together can create conflicts—for instance, enlarging print in a way that exceeds a learner’s safe physical reach.
Addressing only one eligibility label leaves interacting sensory, motor, or health barriers unaddressed and risks unsafe or inaccessible participation.
Diagnostic categories describe broad patterns, not how a specific learner’s multiple needs interact with particular equipment, lighting, acoustics, and positioning.

Correct. Co-occurring disabilities may interact in ways that are not captured by treating each label separately. Collaborative task analysis and trials show how combined access, communication, positioning, and health supports function. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.

items.prompt: During foundational word-reading intervention, a student with dyslexia reads familiar words from memory but struggles to decode new words. Which instruction most directly addresses the need?
choices: Explicit, systematic instruction in phonics, word analysis, and cumulative decoding practice.
Extended independent silent reading time with self-selected books and minimal adult interruption or feedback.
Repeated flashcard drills aimed at memorizing the visual outline of each new grade-level vocabulary word.
Replacing print reading instruction with audio recordings across all literacy and content-area assignments.
items.rationale: Dyslexia commonly involves accurate or fluent word recognition, decoding, and spelling. Explicit, systematic instruction with modeling, guided practice, cumulative review, and feedback directly addresses these skills. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Correct. Dyslexia commonly involves accurate or fluent word recognition, decoding, and spelling. items.prompt: When two learners respond differently to the same instructional tool, two students share the same documented support profile but respond differently to the same scaffold. What should the teacher do?
choices: Maintain uniform instructional scaffolds for both students so accommodations match their shared eligibility category.
Use individual performance data to select, monitor, and adapt supports for each student.

items.rationale: A individual support profile does not prescribe a single instructional profile. Individualized planning uses current performance, preferences, goals, and response data to decide which supports help each learner. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
choiceRationales: Standardizing supports by eligibility label ignores wide within-category variability and contradicts IDEA’s core requirement for individualized programming.

Individualized planning uses current performance, preferences, goals, and response data to decide which supports help each learner. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.
Fairness in special education means providing what each learner needs to access learning, not keeping an ineffective scaffold in place for uniformity.

Correct. Present levels should describe current, measurable academic or functional performance and how disability affects progress. Specific baseline evidence supports goal design and later comparison. For 5322 preparation, connect intellectual and adaptive evidence to individualized, age-respectful instruction; presume competence; integrate communication, functional, academic, social, self-determination, and transition goals; fade support toward agency; and monitor meaningful participation and generalization.

items.prompt: In writing an annual IEP objective, which draft annual IEP goal is written in measurable terms?
choices: With continued special education reading instruction, the student will demonstrate stronger oral reading fluency by spring.

items.prompt: A student is beginning to connect sounds and letters and enjoys shared stories. Which literacy plan is most appropriate?

items.prompt: A student can select a new vocabulary symbol during drill but not during class discussion. How should vocabulary instruction change?

choiceRationales: Memorizing one symbol picture creates a narrow visual association rather than genuine conceptual generalization across real objects and discussions.
